answer.text: Because they derive their value from an underlying asset
Because they are derived from corporate balance sheets each quarter
Because they are settled only through physical delivery of the underlying
Because they always have a positive intrinsic value

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series VIII workbook (pages 59-61), derivatives are financial contracts whose value is derived from an underlying asset such as a stock, index, commodity, or currency. The name reflects this dependence on the underlying. The Trap: Derivatives are not defined by quarterly corporate filings, by physical delivery, or by always having positive intrinsic value; many derivatives are cash settled, and option intrinsic value can be zero. Note: Source: NISM Series VIII workbook, pages 59-61.
